messages.subject: Create several plots and save as files
parts:
I have two questions.

1.  I have a data frame that contains 18 sets of effect estimates that I want to plot with ggplot with this code that was provided by generous members of this forum. Each set contains 7 effect estimates. I want to generate 18 plots and save them as separate files. The following code is created  for rows 1 to 7.

 

ggplot(nox, aes(x = lags, y = est, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) + 

  geom_linerange(position=position_dodge(width=2)) + geom_point(size=3)

  geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=2)) +

  ylab("Odds ratio & 95% CI") +

  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1)) +  xlab('Lag (days)')  +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0:6))+

  xlab('Lag (days)')

 

The second question refers to the error message that accompanies running the code above and it is shown below. The error appears although a plot is created. The plot from the code above is pasted below. What does the error message mean and should I be concerned about it?

 

 

Warning messages:

1: position_dodge requires non-overlapping x intervals

2: position_dodge requires non-overlapping x intervals

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Create several plots and save as files
parts: Hi:

On Sat, Nov 16, 2013 at 6:22 AM, Nicippe B <nic...@gmail.com> wrote:

I have two questions.

1.  I have a data frame that contains 18 sets of effect estimates that I want to plot with ggplot with this code that was provided by generous members of this forum. Each set contains 7 effect estimates. I want to generate 18 plots and save them as separate files. The following code is created  for rows 1 to 7.

 

ggplot(nox, aes(x = lags, y = est, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) + 

  geom_linerange(position=position_dodge(width=2)) + geom_point(size=3)

  geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=2)) +

  ylab("Odds ratio & 95% CI") +

  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1)) +  xlab('Lag (days)')  +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0:6))+

  xlab('Lag (days)')

I don't understand why you need position_dodge(). Typically, you use it in conjunction with a second factor where one factor is used for the x-axis and the levels of the second factor are dodged across each level of the first.

To answer your question more directly, one way is to wrap the plot code into a function. Are you using different data set names with the same variables or do both the input data frames and input variables vary? The answer to that question would inform you about the arguments you need for the function. Secondly, do you have specific output file names in mind for each plot or do you want to construct them from the input data frame name? The answer to that question will dictate whether the output file name should be passed as a function argument or should be constructed inside the function.

The second question refers to the error message that accompanies running the code above and it is shown below. The error appears although a plot is created. The plot from the code above is pasted below. What does the error message mean and should I be concerned about it?

I don't know. If your attached graph is what you want, then remove the position_dodge() stuff in your code and the message will very likely disappear. If you were expecting something else, you should probably mention it.

Let's pretend that all you want to do is switch the file name each time but otherwise you want the same graph to be produced, and it's supposed to look like what you attached. Here's one way to streamline the process a bit.

# 18 file names in a vector - substitute the correct file format
# if csv is incorrect (and of course the names)
filenames <- paste0("file", seq(18), ".csv")

# A function that takes a file name as input but otherwise makes the same plot
ggp <- function(file)
    {
    require(ggplot2)
    p <-  ggplot(get(file), aes(x = lags, y = est, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) + 

      geom_linerange() + geom_point(size=3)

      geom_point() +

ylab("Odds ratio & 95% CI") +

      geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1)) +  xlab('Lag (days)')  +

      scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0:6))+

      xlab('Lag (days)')

# pull out the first part of the filename and attach a

# graphics format to it in the ggsave() call

outroot <- unlist(strsplit(file, "\\."))[1] 

ggsave(p, file = paste0(outroot, ".pdf") 

}


 

library(plyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Recursively apply the function to each file in filenames. The _ in plyr
# means that you do not want to return anything - saving the graph each
# time is a desired 'side effect'.

l_ply(filenames, ggp)
 

There are multiple ways to go about this. It's quite possible this has nothing to do with your situation; if so, you need to post back with further details, and preferably, a small reproducible example. (See the link at the bottom of this post for guidelines.)


Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Create several plots and save as files
parts:
Hi:

One way to go about this is to write a function to get a single plot and to use one of the apply family functions to map it to each sub-data frame associated with unique exposure levels. The plyr package is useful in this regard.

# Function to generate the plot
plotfun <- function(d)
{
   require(ggplot2)
   p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = lags)) +
           geom_pointrange(aes(y = est, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), size = 1)
   pname <- paste0(as.character(d$exposure[1]), ".pdf")
   ggsave(p, file = pname)
   invisible()
}

# Map it to each exposure group: the _ indicates that nothing should be
# saved since a side effect is performed (i.e., saving the graphs)
library(plyr)
d_ply(df, .(exposure), plotfun)

I got three saved plots from this code, as expected. The plot function is simple, so tailor it to your needs.

Dennis

I don't know. If your attached graph is what you want, then remove the position_dodge() stuff in your code and the message will very likely disappear. If you were expecting something else, you should probably mention it.

Let's pretend that all you want to do is switch the file name each time but otherwise you want the same graph to be produced, and it's supposed to look like what you attached. Here's one way to streamline the process a bit.

# 18 file names in a vector - substitute the correct file format
# if csv is incorrect (and of course the names)
filenames <- paste0("file", seq(18), ".csv")

# A function that takes a file name as input but otherwise makes the same plot
ggp <- function(file)
    {
    require(ggplot2)
    p <-  ggplot(get(file), aes(x = lags, y = est, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) + 

      geom_linerange() + geom_point(size=3)

      geom_point() +

      ylab("Odds ratio & 95% CI") +

      geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 1)) +  xlab('Lag (days)')  +

      scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0:6))+

      xlab('Lag (days)')


# pull out the first part of the filename and attach a

# graphics format to it in the ggsave() call

outroot <- unlist(strsplit(file, "\\."))[1] 

ggsave(p, file = paste0(outroot, ".pdf") 

}


 

library(plyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Recursively apply the function to each file in filenames. The _ in plyr
# means that you do not want to return anything - saving the graph each
# time is a desired 'side effect'.

l_ply(filenames, ggp)
 

There are multiple ways to go about this. It's quite possible this has nothing to do with your situation; if so, you need to post back with further details, and preferably, a small reproducible example. (See the link at the bottom of this post for guidelines.)
